cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing to the church in Corinth, where some men are boasting about themselves and want to be seen as his equals (2 Corinthians 10:12; 11:12). Paul has already asked the church to put up with a little foolishness from him (11:1), and now he comes back to it. He says, "I repeat: Let no one take me for a fool." But if they do, then fine, receive him as a fool, so he too may boast a little.

cards.question: Paul's about to boast about himself. True or false: Paul says this confident boasting is the way the Lord would speak.
Paul admits boasting is fool talk. So why does Paul decide to boast at all?

cards.text: Then Paul tells the church they gladly put up with fools, "since you are so wise." I think there's a pinch in that compliment, friend, like when the boss says "bold choice" and walks away slowly.

cards.question: Paul lists what the Corinthians put up with from the boasters. True or false: Paul says they even put up with someone who strikes them in the face.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "To my shame I concede that we were too weak for that!" Friend, that's the most backwards apology I've ever heard: "I'm SO sorry I never pushed you around."

cards.question: Speaking as a fool, Paul says he can ___ what anyone else dares to boast about.

cards.text: And here comes the matching: the boasters are Hebrews and Israelites, and Paul says so is he. Every brag they've got, he's got a "me too" ready to go.

cards.question: One more match from Paul. The boasters claim to be descendants of someone, and Paul says he is too. Who?

cards.text: Paul's still matching the boasters, now on whether they're servants of Christ. Then he adds, "I am speaking as if I were out of my mind."

cards.question: True or false: Paul says that as a servant of Christ, he's only about equal to the boasters.

cards.text: He's so much more, Paul says: in harder labor, in more imprisonments, in worse beatings, in frequent danger of death. Most people brag about promotions, but Paul's brag list is BEATINGS.

cards.question: Paul gets specific about those beatings. Five times he received the same punishment from the Jews. What was it?

cards.text: Paul keeps counting: three times beaten with rods, once stoned, three times shipwrecked.
He even spent a night and a day in the open sea. Friend, I used to complain about the junk drawer, but at least the junk drawer was DRY.

cards.question: On his many journeys, Paul faced danger from rivers, bandits and more. True or false: that includes danger from his own countrymen.
And it's not just danger for Paul. Along with labor and toil, what does Paul say he often went without?
All of that is trouble from the outside. What pressure does Paul say he faces daily?

cards.text: Then Paul asks, "Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn with grief?" That's the friend who hears YOUR bad news and somehow HE'S the one who needs to sit down.

cards.question: If Paul must boast, he says he will boast of the things that show his ___.
Paul brings God into it. True or false: Paul says the God and Father of the Lord Jesus knows he is not lying.

cards.text: In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas, an Arabian king, secured the city of the Damascenes in order to arrest Paul. The whole city, locked down for ONE guy.

cards.question: Damascus is secured and the governor wants Paul arrested. How does Paul escape?

answers.text: Lowered in a basket through a window
Slipped out through the city gate

cards.text: And Paul escaped the governor's grasp. The great apostle gets to boast, and he picks the story where he leaves town in a BASKET, and I LOVE this man.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: the setup about the boasters, Paul's earlier request in 11:1, the quote, and "But if they do, then fine, receive him as a fool, so he too may boast a little." It needs to be cut to 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: Card 1 already says "some men are boasting about themselves." That gives away the right answer to card 3 ("Many are already boasting") and rules out the other two answers before the baker reasons anything out.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card says "Paul's still matching the boasters, now on whether they're servants of Christ." In 11:23 Paul doesn't match them on this point. He says "I am so much more." The setup states something the text shows is untrue, and it steers the baker toward True on card 2.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The question says "Paul gets specific about those beatings," so the answer has to be a beating. "Thrown into a cistern" and "A night in the stocks" are not beatings, so the setup rules them out. The wrong answers also aren't the same kind of thing as the right answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: In 11:29 Paul shares in others' weakness and grieves over their sin. The joke compares him to a friend who hears your bad news and makes it about himself. That is a different action, and it casts Paul as self-centered. It laughs at him instead of with his human situation.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
